18.name: Francis Smith
18.headline: Bring the pads. He plans to use them.
18.bio: Smith likes a straightforward challenge, whether he is assembling furniture without the instructions or arguing that the best meal on campus comes from a tiny breakfast counter. The Ohio State back keeps a stack of handwritten goals beside his bed and enjoys being the teammate who turns a long day into a competition. His Power Back archetype gives the football story a clear direction: a sturdy runner built around a physical identity. The question worth following is how that identity travels when patience, spacing and an unglamorous cut matter more than the collision.
18.watch: Reading the first crease, keeping his feet organized through traffic and choosing when to press the run.

24.name: Jaylan Matthews Jr.
24.headline: Small spaces. Big possibilities.
24.bio: Matthews is the Alabama teammate who can turn waiting for the team bus into a debate, a dance contest or both. He grew up helping an uncle organize community cookouts and still volunteers to handle the music whenever the group gets together. There is a playful confidence to his story, paired with an Elusive Back profile that invites creativity. The next chapter is about putting that imagination on a schedule: recognizing the useful opening, committing to it and saving the extra move for a defender who actually demands one.
24.watch: Decisive cuts, discipline behind the line and turning open-field ideas into efficient decisions.

30.name: Tye Miller
30.headline: An elusive profile with a deliberate mindset
30.bio: Miller's quiet habit is photography: campus corners, empty basketball courts and anything that changes with the light. At Missouri, he is the friend who remembers where everyone left their keys, then becomes unexpectedly relentless over a game of cards. That mix of observation and competition gives his story its personality. The Elusive Back archetype supplies the scouting starting point. What makes this projection interesting is the balance between seeing possibilities and acting on one, especially when a run offers a modest gain before it offers a highlight.
30.watch: Vision, timing behind his blockers and choosing the productive lane over the tempting detour.

43.name: De'Quan Coleman
43.headline: A big back with an appetite for the details
43.bio: Coleman spends his Colorado downtime baking bread, a hobby he picked up from a family recipe book filled with handwritten corrections. He is patient with a slow rise and far less patient with anyone who skips cleaning the kitchen. That demanding, good-humored streak shapes his fictional locker-room identity. At 230 pounds with a Power Back archetype, the outline is easy to see. The useful question goes beyond size: can he keep the run on time, navigate a crowded exchange and make his physical approach fit the blocking in front of him?
43.watch: Tempo, footwork in tight lanes and staying available when the play asks for something beyond the handoff.

67.name: Qualeek Leonard
67.headline: The dimensions say power. The profile invites invention.
67.bio: Leonard has the build to make you check the position label twice: a 230-pound Notre Dame runner listed as an Elusive Back. Away from football, he writes short adventure stories and shares the unfinished chapters with a small circle of friends who are merciless editors. He likes a surprising turn, but he has learned that a story still needs a clear destination. That is a fitting theme for his projection. The intrigue is a larger runner with an elusive identity; the challenge is making every change of direction serve the play.
67.watch: Balance between size and movement, efficient changes of direction and commitment to the designed lane.

83.name: Demond Henderson
83.headline: Compact frame. Plenty to unpack.
83.bio: Henderson is the North Carolina teammate who plans the group outing, double-checks the reservation and still finds a way to get everyone lost looking for dessert. He collects old basketball jerseys and takes friendly arguments about their design much too seriously. His story has an easygoing surface and a competitive center. The 228-pound frame and Elusive Back archetype create an interesting combination. The next step is giving that combination a reliable rhythm, with enough patience to trust a developing lane and enough conviction to stop waiting once it opens.
83.watch: Patience versus hesitation, clean footwork through congestion and consistent decisions at the line.

92.name: Kiaan Brown
92.headline: An outlet with ambitions beyond the checkdown
92.bio: Brown approaches USC life with a sketchbook in his backpack and a running list of restaurants he wants to try with friends. He designs imaginary food-truck menus, complete with names his teammates usually veto. That collaborative, detail-loving personality suits the story of a Receiving Back looking for a defined place in an offense. At 5-foot-8 and 213 pounds, he brings a compact outline to that role. The projection revolves around dependable execution: being where the quarterback expects, understanding the spacing and making the ordinary outlet feel like a purposeful part of the play.
92.watch: Route detail, positioning as an outlet and building a complete role alongside his receiving identity.

1.name: J.T. Rhoads
1.headline: The huddle is his office
1.bio: Rhoads treats the quarterback room like a second major. At USC, he started a weekly film club with his receivers, complete with handwritten quizzes and a strict bring-your-own-breakfast policy. Away from football, he restores old headphones and keeps a notebook of stadium sounds. The personality fits the Field General billing: curious, deliberate and comfortable owning the conversation. The appeal is a quarterback who wants answers before the snap. The next chapter is learning when the perfect answer can wait and a decisive throw cannot.
1.watch: Command of the offense, anticipation and decisive play when the original plan breaks down.

2.name: Jaquon Hall
2.headline: Built to turn a broken play into a problem
2.bio: Hall's Alabama story starts with backyard games where the pocket was whatever space the lawn furniture left open. He still brings that improviser's imagination to a Scrambler profile, but his off-field obsession is surprisingly patient: cooking elaborate Sunday dinners for teammates. He is the loudest voice during competitive games and the first to laugh at his own mistake afterward. The intrigue is obvious: a sturdy quarterback whose style invites movement and invention. The challenge is knowing when the escape hatch is an advantage and when staying on schedule is the bigger play.
2.watch: Pocket discipline, choices outside structure and balancing creation with the routine throw.

6.name: Aaron Archuelta
6.headline: Big frame. Bigger ambitions.
6.bio: Archuelta carries the Strong Arm label and a frame that makes the projection easy to picture. His life away from Penn State football is quieter than that billing: he builds model airplanes, prefers long walks to crowded parties and turns fiercely competitive whenever a board game hits the table. He keeps a tiny model plane in his locker as a reminder that power means little without control. That is the theme of this prospect, too. The attraction is the vertical ambition; the developmental question is whether he can make the underneath game feel just as purposeful.
6.watch: Touch, timing and willingness to take the available completion before hunting the big shot.

14.name: Nick Gardiner
14.headline: A steady hand with something left to prove
14.bio: Gardiner's Notre Dame routine begins with an early coffee and ends with a dog-eared notebook. The redshirt senior collects old mystery novels, coaches a neighborhood trivia team and refuses to leave a disagreement about a movie ending unresolved. He is the patient organizer rather than the speechmaker, a natural match for the Field General archetype. There is a clear identity here: preparation, structure and ownership. The interesting question is how that measured approach translates when a defense forces him to abandon the script.
14.watch: Processing under pressure, rhythm and conviction when the pocket or coverage changes late.

56.name: Nick Barrientos
56.headline: The bet is on the arm—and the imagination
56.bio: Barrientos brings a Strong Arm archetype to a Miami story with plenty of color. He sketches sneaker designs in the margins of his notebooks, DJs small get-togethers for teammates and insists every road trip needs a carefully sequenced playlist. The creative streak also defines his football personality: he likes possibilities, especially the ambitious ones. That makes for an intriguing developmental canvas. The next step is turning imagination into a repeatable process, with the patience to let a simple completion do useful work.
56.watch: Consistency of decisions, controlled aggression and execution on the ordinary downs.

63.name: Zac Williams
63.headline: A patient competitor chasing his opening
63.bio: Williams' Ohio State backstory centers on persistence rather than a ready-made spotlight. He spends free afternoons repairing bicycles, has a dry joke for every tense meeting and keeps a list of small tasks he wants to master each month. He is not the loudest player in the room, but he has no interest in being background scenery. The Strong Arm archetype gives his profile its starting point. His next chapter is about making that tool part of a complete routine: timing, touch and the discipline to keep a drive alive.
63.watch: Repeatable mechanics, rhythm throws and using arm strength without forcing the issue.
